title: On OpenCode the holder of a dispatched unit is unnameable while it holds it — the plugin sees the child's session id first and could claim for it

labels.name: fr:in-progress
labels.description: An agent is actively working on this

body:
## Summary

On OpenCode, the agent holding a dispatched unit cannot be named **while it holds it**. The task tool blocks and returns the child session id only with the result, so `fr run claim --agent <id>` can only happen after the phase is over. During the phase, `fr run status` reads:

```
HELD BY an unclaimed agent (opencode, <model>) since …
```

#527 made fr *say* this truthfully (parity row `dispatch-holder-identity`: `opencode: partial`; the fr-goal skill now says a blocking dispatch is claimed on return). It did not close the gap. This issue is the gap.

Evidence: `docs/acceptance/evidence/2026-09-21-pr508-live-test-plan.md`, caveat C1 — the orchestrator reported learning the id "only when the task tool returned", and the status above was captured from *inside* the child, because the orchestrator could not look.

## Why it matters

#503's whole point was answering "who is holding phase 2 **right now**" — the question you have when a phase has run for an hour and you cannot tell whether its agent is alive. On OpenCode the answer today is *harness and model, never which agent*. What still works, and must keep working: the open record refuses a second dispatch whether or not anyone claimed it.

## The opening

`packages/fr-opencode-plugin` already has both halves:

- it sees a `sessionID` on every `tool.execute.before` call, the child's included;
- `src/idle.ts` already tells a child session from a top-level one (`isTopLevel`).

So on a **child** session's first tool call, the plugin knows the id the orchestrator will not learn until the end, at exactly the moment it becomes useful.

## What it would take

1. **A CLI affordance to claim without naming the unit.** The plugin knows a session id, not a step or item. Something like `fr run claim <run> --open-unit --agent <id>`: claim *the one* open, unclaimed attempt; refuse (exit 2, naming them) when there are zero or several. Phase executors run serially in one workspace, so "the one" is well defined — and the refusal is what keeps it honest when it is not.
2. **The plugin hook**: child session + first tool call + an fr run on this branch → call it once. Fail-open, silent, once per session — the same posture as the idle adapter.
3. **Finding the run** from the plugin's cwd: `fr run check --idle --format json` already resolves a run from a workspace; reuse that, do not re-derive it.

## Why this is an issue rather than a PR

It cannot be live-verified from a Claude Code session, and the repo's standard (gh#494) is that a plugin behaviour is not `enforced` until a real OpenCode session shows it executing — a green `bun test` does not. It would ship `partial`, like `fr-run-idle-guard`'s OpenCode cell, until someone drives it.

**Also unknown:** whether Hermes has the same shape. `delegate_task`'s handle timing has never been observed; the parity cell says so rather than guessing.

## Related

- **#503 / #508** — the dispatch holder record.
- **#527** — C1: made the declaration true; the parity cell's `scope_note` points here ("A plugin-side claim on the child's first tool call would close this; not built").
- **#522** — the matrix cannot express "owed a live run on harness H", which is what this would be on landing.
